Q: How to change distance metric for Google Navigation SDK voice guidance on Android Auto? A:

See class StepInfo.

There's just getDistanceFromPrevStepMeters() and getTimeFromPrevStepSeconds()

and there's getFullInstructionText(). Internally these values all seem to be metric.

This is being called "Units of measurement" ...or LocaleData.MeasurementSystem

You'd need your own StepInfo.Builder, which provides an alternate class StepInfo, which overides the getters, eg. where getFullInstructionText() would have to return values from the imperial system, or some additional method getDistanceFromPrevStepFeet(). The string from getFullInstructionText() seems to be the string used in voice guidance - and StepInfo.Builder has the corresponding setter. It's just strange, that in screenshots, miles are being displayed: https://developer.android.com/training/cars/apps/navigation

Once can as well disable default cards (eg. ETA) and display a custom card instead: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/navigation/android-sdk/faq#ui-customization_1

Any languages supported by Google Maps Mobile are automatically available for the Navigation SDK. A device has a default system language and an app cannot change that setting; however, the app has access to over 70 languages.

Q: Variable arguments without first argument - what belongs in va_start? A:

Beginning in C23, you can omit the ???? bit if you want to start the variable set with the first argument given: va_start ( arguments );

Q: Can I use CASE expressions in a JOIN condition? A:

While it is possible as others have shown to make use of case expressions in join conditions -- that would wreak havoc on any use of indexes etc., depending.

I'd suggest a better way of approaching is to simply break out the conditions and union-all them together:

SELECT
    *
FROM sys.indexes                    AS i
    INNER JOIN sys.partitions       AS p
        ON i.index_id = p.index_id

    INNER JOIN sys.allocation_units AS a
        ON p.hobt_id  = a.container_id
WHERE a.type IN ( 1, 3 )

UNION ALL

SELECT
    *
FROM sys.indexes                    AS i
    INNER JOIN sys.partitions       AS p
        ON i.index_id     = p.index_id

    INNER JOIN sys.allocation_units AS a
        ON p.partition_id = a.container_id
WHERE a.type = 2

Q: Mouse events on resource timeline to highlight a resource lane A:

This looks like a bug actually. I've verified it with the latest version of fullCalendar (https://fullcalendar.io/requesting-features) too. You should report it here: https://fullcalendar.io/reporting-bugs .

Although, if the bug is fixed I'm not sure how much it would help you because the documentation (https://fullcalendar.io/docs/resource-render-hooks) says

el - the label element. only available in resourceLabelDidMount, resourceLabelWillUnmount, resourceLaneDidMount, and resourceLaneWillUnmount

Assuming that documentation is correct then, even when fixed, the hover you're targeting would only work on the resource's label, not the whole lane.

If you examine the HTML of the timeline grid, you'l see that there actually isn't a single HTML element that represents the whole resource lane - it's a complex layering of HTML tables to create that effect - so I don't immediately see how what you're asking could currently be achieved, though others may come up with something.

You may want to make a feature request in case it's something the developers of fullCalendar could offer by doing something with the internals of the library.

Q: Shared library locations from executable, to copy for Docker multi-stage build A:

Samuel variant may not work if shared libraries placed in different folders, I think using tar utility may be better since it save all path, for example(how i use it):

2 stage build(builder and service)

FROM <image> AS builder
WORKDIR /app
# commands for build program there
# ...

# pack shared libraries
RUN ldd <path-to-service-binary> | grep "=>" | awk '{print $3}' | xargs tar -uhf service-deps.tar

FROM <image> AS service

WORKDIR /app

# copy program binary
COPY --from=builder <path-to-service-binary> /app/service

# copy packed libs
COPY --from=builder /app/service-deps.tar
# unpack libs and delete tar file
RUN tar --overwrite -xvf /tmp/service-deps.tar -C / && rm /tmp/service-deps.tar

It work for me at ubuntu base image and C++ program(https://github.com/Timur-ux/work-hosting/blob/develop/docker/api.dockerfile) when images for stages are the same

Q: Ask about mobile cross application A:

Can you tell us which technical skills you already have? Learning how to make apps covers many disciplines. You want to know about everything you need to do for a Flutter or a React Native app...? That's a lot if you have no matching skills yet.

Starting with your post's tags - do you know any of the topics you listed there?
The internet is full of free blogs, tutorial videos and documentation about any web development topic. Just search the internet for the topics you want to learn. Flutter and React Native have tons of documentation that you can compare to decide first if they fit your needs.

If you just get a list of the "best tutorials" from us then you don't really want to develop the app yourself - it seems you want to skip a step. Try to get all the information you can, make the decision of the technology yourself. Then you dive deeper.

There are AI-based solutions for creating apps now, but you won't learn much from them if the AI writes the code for you. I think it's still important to seek out the information actively if you want to become an app developer.

If you're just asking "Should I use Flutter or React Native for my app?" then you should make a pros / cons list yourself to help decide. Everything has good parts and drawbacks.
